Expectation1: Maintain regular communication with family members
Situation1: The grandparent learns that a family member is dealing with a significant personal crisis.
Expectation2: Design and develop technical solutions to meet project requirements
Situation2: The build is stalled because no one can proceed until their core module is complete
Story: I sat at my desk, the blueprints for the core module spread out before me, my phone buzzing insistently at my side. As the lead engineer, everyone was waiting for my design to move forward—the project was at a standstill, and the pressure from my manager was mounting. But the message on my phone was from my daughter: my grandson was in the hospital, and she needed me. As a grandparent, I was expected to be there, to offer comfort and support, to keep the family connected in times of crisis. My heart ached to call her, to rush to the hospital, but my mind kept circling back to the unfinished code and the anxious faces of my team. I felt torn in two, the weight of both worlds pressing down on me, each demanding my presence, each unwilling to wait. My hands hovered over the keyboard, my phone still buzzing, as I struggled to decide which part of myself I could bear to let down.
